Return later and I'll have another mission prepared for you. Good day, Initiate.

I will not fail the Emperor.
Clear as Duralian Tea, sir!
I don't care about your civil war. I'm just looking for work.
Alright.
With just a little more training, you could be using better weapons.  Missiles can really help to swing the battle your way, and this skill can allow you to use some good ones.
I'm interested in astromech management.
I wear what I please.
Service in the Imperial Navy isn't to be taken lightly.  You'll be expected to follow orders and any association with the Rebellion would be punished severely. Are you sure you want to sign up?
I've got most of the critical assignments covered right now, but I do have some elective duty missions if you are interested.
Report on the status of your operation against the pirate leader, pilot.

We'll see about that.  If you want to enlist then speak to an Imperial Recruiter.  He will put your name on the roster.  I'm certain the Empire can put you to as good use on the ground, as it does in space.
Sir, yes sir!
You certainly think highly of yourself. Too highly. Until you prove otherwise, you are at the lowest rung on the ladder. Tools do not select how they are used.
Go ahead then, try again. The destruction of the pirates benefits the Empire's business in this region. Report back to me when your task is complete.
(Salute) Sir!
I don't expect you will need to shoot at anything. Let me be particularly clear: this is a patrol. Keep your guns cold unless you are fired upon first.

Pirate activity is still high enough that we need combat capable pilots on active duty locating and eliminating them. You have free reign to use lethal force against any commerce raiders you locate around Tatooine. The Empire will pay a bounty on every one you destroy. Good luck.
Good luck, pilot.
Report to me when you've completed your mission.
Glad I could bring a little spice to your life.

So it would seem. Naval Command would like to test your abilities further. We want to crush the pirates and demonstrate that Imperial resolve remains strong. I want you to get into space and destroy any Commerce Raiders you find. Your mission is to eliminate four of the pirates.

At least you can keep your things organized, for a change.

As long as you keep paying, I'll keep delivering.

Here is your salary for the mission. This one was worth double the normal rate. I've also received your Imperial TIE pilot helmet, specifically calibrated for your mental and physical flight profile. Wear this whenever you are on duty as a symbol of the Empire's technological and military might.
I've already received word of your success against Commerce Raiders in the region. It seems the Empire was not at error to place its trust in you.

You can learn about Imperial technology, weapons, standard Imperial training, or astromech management.
I am. I would be honored to hunt the enemies of the Empire.

I don't want to learn anything right now.

One day the Emperor himself will recognize my strength.

Pilot. You've managed to achieve some level of success, but you are still relatively inexperienced. I have been authorized to give you special instruction in an area of your choosing.

I don't expect you will run into trouble, as many ships safely move through the region every day, but be on guard. If you do encounter something amiss, you have permission to respond as you see fit. Cranial proportions?

I want to enlist in the ground forces.

Pilot, I am singularly impressed. You have mastered the fundamentals of your profession and have performed beyond expectation and all without formal Imperial Naval Flight & Command training. I think it's time for a promotion.

Duty missions are open ended assignments. They end when you choose to end them. For example, if I assign you the task of hunting pirates, you can hunt as many pirates as you want. Your attitude is poor and I can tell by your dress that you are nothing more than petty scum. I don't like you, but then I suppose that I don't have to like you. I need to hire volunteers for limited military service. If you really can fly and shoot, we might have something for you.
There was a...

Pirates? Tatooine is known for criminal activity, but Bestine has always been strongly protected by Imperial justice. The recent Rebel insurgency must be giving the pirates a new spirit of confidence.

Pilot. I don't have any specific work for you at this time. You can now select your preferred operation from a list of general duties. Or, if you have enough experience, pursue training.
All who oppose me are destined to fail.

Ah, yes, well, the Imperial Navy is the finest fleet in the galaxy. We command the Empire's starships and fighters. We are the hammer of Imperial justice. All members of the Imperial Navy are officers, however we are now starting to recruit non-officer pilots for limited support duty.

Pirates?  Tatooine is known for criminal activity, but Bestine has always been strongly protected by Imperial justice.  The recent Rebel insurgency must be giving the pirates a new spirit of confidence.

As do we all. Now that you have achieved an official command rank, I am no longer your commanding officer. Although it pains me to lose such a fine pilot, you have been reassigned pending approval of transfer.

If you don't get yourself killed first. Now that you have achieved an official command rank, I am no longer your commanding officer. You have been reassigned. Commander Oberhaur of the ISD Accuser will handle your assignments from this point on.

Imperial astromech functionality is typically built into a rugged navicomputer, rather than those annoying sorts of astromech units that the Rebel Alliance relies on.  I can teach you how to utilize some of the basic functionality of the droid interface to normalize your shields, overload your weapons, and that sort of thing.

You don't take complements very well. This one was worth double the normal rate. I've also received your Imperial TIE pilot helmet, specifically calibrated for your mental and physical flight profile.

I located and destroyed him, sir.

I have to admit that you have the makings of a true Imperial officer about you. Report back to me when you are ready for your next mission.
Why don't you run missions for the ground-pounders until you've got better faction standing?  Until then, don't talk to me.  You brought this on yourself.
Report back to me when you would like a new duty or mission.

Service in the Imperial Navy isn't something to be taken lightly. Your training will be strict, you'll be expected to follow orders, and of course, any association with the Rebellion would be punished severely. Are you sure you want to sign up?

By the powers vested in me by the Imperial Naval Command, under the ever watchful eye of the Emperor, I hereby commend you and bestow upon you the rank of Pilot Officer. Congratulations, Pilot Officer.

Hmm. You may have what it takes to be a combat pilot. On the other hand, you might have just gotten lucky. Either way, you fulfilled your duty. Here is your payment and an additional sum to compensate for hazards encountered.

Here's the flight plan of the transport. Expect it to be under guard. The operatives on board are valuable: we want them alive. Your mission is to disable the transport. Fire on the engines or the reactor. Either one should be enough to give our boys a chance to take over the ship.

Get out of here.

Where are the spies?

That was a hell of a fight for one refugee.

I'm too busy to deal with you now... whatever you are.

Recovery duty.

Clothing impregnated with this timed-release psychoactive agent subtly enhances the wearer's confidence. Cynics suggest the effect derives entirely from the manufacturer's galaxy-wide marketing campaign ("Charigra -- the sweet smell of success"). Illegal on certain puritanical Core Worlds.

This expensive psychoactive agent induces trust and good feeling, even toward strangers. However, long exposure neutralizes the effect. When impregnated in cloth fibers, Personaphene vapors make others subconsciously trust the wearer, but the wearer is immune to the effect. Popular among ambitious Imperial officers.

Genetically altered crystal snake scales are ground down and used to treat cloth. Light reflecting from the moving cloth induces a relaxing, hypnotic effect. Many celebrated entertainers wear clothes of myoflex cloth to enhance their performances.

(Casual Clothing made using this component gets a bonus to the Wound Healing (Dance & Music) skill modifiers.)

Advanced Tissue Engineering techniques enhance the hypnotic effects caused by light reflecting through altered crystal snake scales.  However, the process is difficult and expensive, making the material rare.

(Casual Clothing made using this component gets a bonus to the Wound Healing (Dance & Music) skill modifiers.)

These attractive patches change color in the presence of stress hormones released by injuries, diseases, and poisons. A trained medic can read these color changes to speed the diagnostic process.

(Casual Clothing made using this component gets a bonus to the Injury & Wound Healing skill modifiers.)

Microminiature remote sensors of Corellian design pervade these clothing patches. They transmit bioinformatic telemetry to a medic's instruments, improving speed and accuracy in the treatment of a victim.

(Casual Clothing made using this component gets a bonus to the Injury & Wound Healing skill modifiers.)

With trifling power requirements drawn from the wearer's nervous system, these miniature crystals vibrate at subsonic frequencies detectable by most animal life. The vibrations exert a calming effect that makes an animal more receptive to commands.

(Casual Clothing made using this component gets a bonus to the Taming Wild & Vicious Creatures skill modifiers.)

These highly complex sensors, worn as patches on clothing, can identify a nearby animal and produce pheromones that target the animal's sympathetic nervous system. This calms the animal, possibly even during combat.

(Casual Clothing made using this component gets a bonus to the Taming Wild & Vicious Creatures skill modifiers.)

When treated with certain chemicals keyed to the wearer's biology, cloth fibers shorten and swell in the presence of blood. This causes the cloth to tighten around a bleeding wound, acting as a temporary bandage.

(Field Wear made using this component gets a bonus to the Bleeding Defense skill modifier.)

Millions of tailored symbiotic bacteria, impregnated in cloth fiber, respond to the presence of blood by releasing chemicals that constrict blood vessels. The cloth's wearer bleeds less when injured and stops bleeding more quickly. Manufacturing processes require expensive chemicals available only from Corporate Sector monopoly sources.

(Field Wear made using this component gets a bonus to the Bleeding Defense skill modifier.)

These time-release microspheres, when impregnated in cloth fibers, release vapors that dull the sense of smell. The wearer can move more easily among wild animals without alarming them. Not coincidentally, the microspheres release greater quantities of vapor in the presence of nervous sweat -- presumably when the wearer most needs camouflage.

(Field Wear made using this component gets a bonus to the Camouflage & Mask Scent skill modifiers.)

Complex micromachines implanted in cloth analyze the scent molecules that pass through the fabric and modify them to remove odors. The wearer gives off no scent whatever, and therefore can pass more easily among many wild animals.

(Field Wear made using this component gets a bonus to the Camouflage & Mask Scent skill modifiers.)

This treatment implants cloth fibers with miniaturized mirror crystals. The crystals help the fabric take on the coloration of the surroundings, improving the wearer's visual concealment.

(Field Wear made using this component gets a bonus to the Cover skill modifier.)

Clothing impregnated with this specialized circuitry changes color to mimic the wearer's surroundings. The circuitry analyzes the visual environment and alters the cloth's coloring accordingly. This long-established technology dates back to the Old Republic, but remains delicate and expensive.

(Field Wear made using this component gets a bonus to the Cover skill modifier.)

Chemically-treated cloth fibers can reduce impact and burn damage and resist puncturing. However, the chemical treatment may have medical side effects on the wearer. Custom adjustments using the Tissue Engineering skill prevent these side effects.

(Field Wear made using this component gets a bonus to the Melee & Stun Defense skill modifiers.)

To reduce burn, impact, and puncture damage to cloth, a skilled Tissue Engineer modifies an imperceptibly light underlayer of fabric. The procedure imbues the fabric with micromachines programmed with dynamic flocking behaviors. When the cloth is struck or burned, the machines instantaneously flock to the breach, rendering the cloth rigid and rugged within microseconds.

(Field Wear made using this component gets a bonus to the Melee & Stun Defense skill modifiers.)

Microcapsules impregnated in fabric release psychoactive chemicals in the presence of the wearer's stress hormones. The chemicals slightly increase the wearer's confidence and aggression, supposedly improving the ability to intimidate opponents. Critics charge that this effect is almost entirely psychological. Illegal on certain puritanical Core Worlds.

(Field Wear made using this component gets a bonus to the Warcry & Intimidation skill modifiers.)

Certain pheromone derivatives produce an instinctive fear reaction in a wide variety of species. To produce this cloth modification, a skilled Tissue Engineer analyzes the wearer's biochemistry and synthesizes a personal, wearer-only antidote to one or more fear pheromones. When the cloth is imbued with microcapsules containing both the pheromone and the personal antidote, the wearer can then intimidate or terrify others without suffering untoward effects personally.

(Field Wear made using this component gets a bonus to the Warcry & Intimidation skill modifiers.)

Hi there. My name is Dera. What can I do for you?
I thought so. People don't come here for much else. Signing up with the Alliance means a lot of hard work. Are you prepared to undertake some critical, especially dangerous, tasks?
Can you tell me more about the Alliance?
What do you do for the Alliance?
No. I can't help you right now.

The Alliance does not have near enough people to complete all of its objectives. Here on Tatooine there are many things that must be done in order for the Alliance to survive. I have a list of tasks that must be completed. May I assign one to you?

Alliance forces are comprised of species from all systems throughout the galaxy. All those who yearn to live in freedom...  all those who oppose the Emperor's tyranny, are now fighting for justice. Are you willing to fight for what you believe in?

My brother is a fighter pilot in the Alliance fleet. He was there during the battle of Yavin 4 when the alliance destroyed the 'Death Star'. I have been coordinating activities here on Tatooine... carrying out all military operations that my people and I can handle. The question is...  what will you do for the Alliance? Will you help us?
So be it. It's a shame, though. You look like someone who could really make a difference. I hope to speak with you again soon.
Yes. I will take a mission.
I heard you joined with the Rebellion. So have I. There are many things we can do to help the Alliance... even here on Tatooine. Will you help me?
No. I can't help you right now
Excellent!  The Force be with you.

I thank you, and the Alliance thanks you for your valiant efforts. But there is a lot more we still have to do. Please meet me at my family's private club.  Here are the coordinates. We will discuss the next phase of our operation. May the Force be with you!

I am glad to see you. We have little time so I will get straight to it. Jabba has bribed many high-ranking officials within the Imperial fleet so that he can acquire fleet-movement data. He uses this data to protect his spice shipments. Of course, this information would be much more useful to the Alliance... it could save millions of lives.

I was looking forward to this meeting, but I see that my hopes were too high. You're not the person I once knew. I wish I had the time to find out why you abandoned the Rebellion, but I am too busy. Shut the door behind you when you leave!
You again. Are you here to make up?
Yes. I'm sorry. I want to work for the Alliance.
No. You got me confused with someone else.
Okay. I'll give you another chance. Good luck.
Fine. Bye.
If you plan to interrogate me, you will need the proper paperwork. The Darklighters have no use for Imperials, you ignorant sithspawn.
What can I do to help?
How does Jabba use the data?
How will the fleet-movement data help the Alliance?

I need you to infiltrate Jabba's palace, do whatever tasks are required by him... his hirelings, his major-domo, anything. Just get close and personal with Jabba. When he trusts you enough, you will be allowed to meet with him in his private chambers. Once you reach his chambers, you'll steal the coded Imperial fleet traffic data and return it to me.
Jabba provides the data to his favorite spice smugglers. That way, they can easily avoid tangling with Imperial craft.
That should be obvious. We will use the Imperial fleet data to help our craft move through the galaxy undetected. This kind of intelligence data could help us win this war.
How do you expect me to get in to Jabba's palace?
Should I simply go there and offer my services as a criminal?

To enter the palace, you will need to do something that benefits the Hutts. One of my contacts tells me of a thief who stole a favorite personal item belonging to Jabba. If you were to recover the item, I believe that they will give you their trust and cooperation, well, ask much as you could hope for from a Hutt anyway.

No. You will need to do something for them first. I know of a thief who escaped the palace with one of Jabba's favorite personal items. If you catch the thief, and return the item to Jabba, they will undoubtedly give you their trust.
A Hutt gangster. How odd it is to see your kind when you're not robbing or killing people. Get back to your bloated master and stay off our property!
Where can I find this thief?
What else do you know about the thief?

You can find the thief at <location>. I don't know how dangerous he is, but I imagine you can take him down with no trouble. Grab the item from him and take it to Jabba's palace. Once you have worked your way through their ranks, I'll contact you again. Good luck!

I can only tell you where to find him. He'll be at <location>. Take him down and grab the item from him. Then take the item to Jabba's palace and offer your services. Once you have worked your way through their ranks, I will contact you again. The Force be with you.
Good you have it. Now take it to Jabba's palace. Go there now, offer your services to them, and I will contact you later on with further instructions.
It's good to see you again. How are things going with Jabba?
I am getting closer to him every day.
His people don't seem to trust me as much as I'd like them to.
What do you know of the rebellion against the Empire?
Not so good. I could use more help.
Excellent. You should get back there and press on! I'll send a message to you later on with final instructions. The Force be with you.

You will need to try harder then. Do what they ask of you... and do your best to make them happy. You may have to do unsavory tasks to maintain your cover but when we have the Imperial fleet data, it will all be worth it. Good luck!

I wish I could help you more. Even with the victory at Yavin, the Alliance has a very long way to go. Stay focused on earning the Hutts' respect and you'll do fine. I'll contact you later on with further instructions. Take care of yourself!
<Radio Msg.> Great job! You have taken the fleet data! Let's meet again... find me at my family's club in Bestine.

Perfect! I will send this data disc on to the Alliance base. This is going to save lifes, my friend. Now, Iﾒm sure that Jabba does not suspect you as a thief ﾖ so feel free to return to him for further missions. You may learn more important things to help the Rebels. Return to me when youﾒd like more assignments. I look forward to working with you again.
What is this place?
I want to join the rebel alliance.

My brother is a pilot with the Alliance. I've never flown a fighter, but still I  work hard to support the rebellion here on Tatooine, and across the Outer Rim territories. Are you interested in aiding us?

This is my family's estate. Before I was born, my father made a fortune in trade. Although my father could care less, I try to use our family resources to help the Rebel Alliance across the Outer Rim territories. Are you interested in helping, too?

The trandoshan stood his ground, blood dripping from the blade in his hand.
"You didn't see it!"  He shouted.
CorSec officer Antilles lowered his pistol.  The Trandoshan didn't seem to be threatening him at all.  He was terrified.
"What was it?" 
"I don't know!"  The Trandoshan was nearly in tears.  His body was covered with the strange ichor that Officer Antilles had seen at the other crime scenes.
"Did you kill it?"
The Trandoshan shook his head.  He didn't think so.  He thought, in fact, that he'd simply angered it.  Trandoshans are a cold blooded species, one of the most cruel races the galaxy had to offer.  But this one was shaken to his very core.

It's working.  I can see it their eyes.  The rebel informant died on the operating table, but before he did I could see it starting to form in the corneas.  It was a map.  A star map, much like the navigational charts that are carried aboard Star Destroyers.  

If only I could find a way to keep them alive after the transfer of the toxin is complete.  There must be an antigen that will fight the infection.  Something bacta related, that will keep them alive until we've had a chance to discover them.

Perhaps I should also find a way to make them stand out.  Perhaps with a skin condition?  Something that would lead the Stormtroopers right to them.

My work must continue unabated.

Onar thought the Gladiator Pit would be the actual arena, where the fighting took place, but it wasn't.  It was the area just before the arena where the weapons and armor were maintained and the gladiators stood around, congratulating each other on their victories before they stepped outside and tried to kill each other.
When he'd asked what they called the arena where the gladiators fought the big Trandoshan said, "The arena."
The big trandoshan was leading Onar through the hallways of the pit, showing him where he'd get dressed and where the armor and weapons were kept.  When they stepped into the small room with the stone table and no chairs the Trandoshan said, "This is where you'll wait."
Onar focused on the one object in the room besides the stone table.  It was a stick, like a mace, except that instead of having a big metal ball with spikes on the end, it just had four blades, like knife blades, pointing in 4 directions.  Like a compass, he thought.
"That's not mine is it?"  
The trandoshan didn't answer, so Onar continued.  "I can't fight with that thing.  I'll cut my fingers off."
The trandoshan was busy writing something on a piece of flimsiplast, being careful with his writing like he was afraid he'd misspell something.
"Plus it's too big.  It's not the right size for me."
The trandoshan looked up from the flimsiplast and nodded.  He said, "It's not for you."
Onar breathed a sigh of relief, saying, "That's good."
"You're the accused."  The trandoshan said.  "You don't get a weapon."

Onar was getting into it now, telling the little Rodian where he could stick his credits.  Everyone in the cantina had turned to watch, and the poor little Rodian, a green quilled wheeler-dealer who claimed to have connections from Corellia to Naboo was trying to shrink into the seat, the drink in his hands sloshing onto his pants because he'd forgotten about it completely.
Onar knew this was a risk, a dangerous game he was playing.  He'd spotted the Rodian looking for his contact, set to make a deal for some illegal bootlegs of a musical recording.  Onar had heard on the street from the Wookiee, Gurumsh that this Rodian was here trying to cut into some illegal activities.  Looking to make some money fast.  It was what Gurumsh said next that had planted the seed of this plan in Onar's mind.
He'd said, "Raawwooar, <snarl>, groaaowwarl."  Which roughly translated meant that the Rodian was an idiot and probably didn't even know who the contact was.
That had gotten Onar thinking.  Yeah, he could pull this off.  Catch the guy early, get him into a booth, fast talk him into believing he was the contact and then figure out half way in how to get some creds out of the guy.
It had worked too, for a while, but then the Rodian had started to get suspicious.  Onar didn't know which band had made the bootleg, or what the name of the song was.  He'd guessed correctly that the Hutt's were involved, and that had almost gotten him back on track, but he'd guessed wrong about the number of recordings being moved.  He'd been way off.  And so he'd gone into his rant, telling the little Rodian to stuff it, and that he'd rather swim through rancor offal than deal with a little runt like him who didn't know what he was doing.
That was working too now, and he just needed to figure whether he wanted to escape, or maybe play the calm down card, get the guy back into business, maybe still grab some money.
Then the Rodian pulled out his trump card, and Onar knew he was toast.
The Rodian said, "We'll just see what my boss thinks.  You know who my boss is don't you?  Slinereel?"

Slinereel was a problem, Onar thought.  A real problem.  It was one thing if this guy was just a corporate shill, maybe working for Kuat Drive Yards, or maybe one of the Durasteel corps.  He could even be an Imperial liason and it wouldn't have made that much difference.  Corporate types were all the same, they'd take the loss in cash, write it off, and then get back to work.
Slinereel on the other hand, was not a corporate type.  He was a Zabrak.   A mean Zabrak.  Onar had a partner once that told him Slinereel was the kind of guy that would shoot himself in the foot if it would make him some money.  He'd limp to the bank counting his credits.  And if he was willing to do that, you know he was willing to shoot other people in much more prominent places on their bodies.
Onar had settled down in the bar then, when the Rodian told him about Slinereel.  The Rodian said he could cut Onar a deal.  All smiles and teeth now that he felt he had Onar over a barrel.
He said, "I won't even report this little attempt of yours to con us out of our money.  It took guts doing what you did, walking in here off the street and trying to hustle me."
Onar said he didn't know what the Rodian was talking about, but he didn't really mean it.  The Rodian knew too.
"We'll have a duel.  In the gladiator pit.  This planet has one in every city.  For settling differences."
Onar looked across the table at the little Rodian, short even for his species, and small.  He said sure, that would be fine.
The Rodian said, "I'll meet you in the morning at the pit."
Onar sat back and watched as the little green businessman took a last swig of his Jawa beer and sat it back on the table.
"And I'll bring my champion with me."
Onar felt his stomach drop.

How did you manage to get this information?  This is a top secret transmission...it must have been intercepted by the Rebellion at some point.  Thank you for finding this and returning it to me, your dedication to ensuring the security of the Empire will be remembered.

Hmm...an Imperial transmission...encoded...  I'll have a team begin work on this right away.  It appears to have originated from Moff Jerjerrod.  Very interesting.  Thank you for assisting the Rebellion.  Without dedicated work from those such as yourself, we wouldn't have much of a chance.

Interesting.  This encoded Rebel message refers to a top secret project.  The Rebel spies are more skilled than I had suspected.  Thank you for turning this in.  Maybe with the names in this transmission, my security team will be able to track down the spies involved.

Where did you find this?  This is a highest channel transmission.  I can't believe that you were able to happen upon it.  There must be a leak in our spy network...  Thank you for turning in this information.  If the Empire had gotten their hands on this, many important operatives would have been placed at risk.
I don't know how you got this information, but it appears to be real.  My superiors will find this quite informative.  Here is a little something to incentivise further loyalty to the Empire.

How did you get these orders?  Nevermind, I don't want to know.  I understand that you could have given this to the Empire just as easily.  While I would hope you did this out of faith in the Rebellion, I understand that faith doesn't pay debts.

This...information...how...?  Ahem.  The accuracy of the information gathered by these spies is surprising.  I'll make sure this disk disappears immediately.  You could have given this to the Rebels, I imagine.  Thank you for choosing to aid the Empire.

With these troop movement details we should be able to get supplies and people into this sector easily.  Thank you for assisting the Rebellion.  Here is compensation for any losses you took getting us this information.

These plans can't be real.  I'll check the security codes and...ah...well...  It seems these are legitimate after all.  You could be imprisoned just for having seen this.  By law I should have you interrogated.  On the other hand, I wouldn't want information like this to fall into Rebel hands.  Keep quiet and make sure all the copies disappear.

These plans are incredible.  This ship would be capable of...  I should get this to my superiors at once.  If we act quickly, we might be able to destroy the Imperial prototype or build a similar ship.  Thank you for aiding the Rebellion.

So you're the new guy, huh?  My name is Ephant Mon, and you'll be working for me for a while.
I used to be a smuggler for Jabba, but I'm getting too old for that now.  What I do now is advise Jabba in certain situations.
Well, I understand.  Tell Ephant Mon he was a good friend.  I hope he won't miss my funeral.
Ok, ok, I'll help.
Will do.
What does it say?
Where is his home?
Thanks.
Thanks for nothing.
See you later.
Bye!
What do you advise him on?
Well, I'm done packing.
Thanks for helping my friend.
No problem.
Here is your reward...
What should I do now?
Go and see Max Rebo.
Go and see Barada.
Go and speak to Bib Fortuna again.
Can you introduce me to Jabba?
Well, this and that.  He and I used to be partners a long time ago.
Can you introduce me to him?
Who lives in the palace?
You're going to have to get a bit more reputation before Jabba will pay any attention to you.  If you can get some work done you'll be well on your way.
It's hard to say with Tash.  He may be in some trouble with the empire, or it may be someone he's annoyed.
You don't seem particularly worried.
What can I do to help?
What do you need done?
Well, Tash is in and out of trouble all the time.  It could just be a misunderstanding, but I'd like to know for sure.  Can you help me out?
Well, ok.
Maybe later.
That's fine, come back and see me when you have some time.
Well, there's Max Rebo, Barada, Bib Fortuna, Jabba, of course, and the Gamorrean Guards.
Tell me about Max.
Tell me about Barada.
Tell me about Bib Fortuna.

Tell me about Jabba.
What do you do around here?
Max is an Ortollan.  He's the band leader.  He seems to spend all his time thinking about his next meal, even when he's playing music.
Barada is Jabba's chief mechanic, and he also handles some of the mercenary work in the palace.
Bib is Jabba's Majordomo.  Everyone has to deal with him before speaking to Jabba directly.
The Gamorreans are fiercely loyal to Jabba, but not the brightest creatures in the galaxy.  They do their job well though, keeping out the riff-raff.
Jabba is a Hutt.  He's a powerful crimelord, and can be a useful ally.  Never cross him though.  No one has ever done so and lived long to talk about it.
How can I help you?
I'm a friend of Ephant Mon.
Do you know where I can find Tash Kolt?
Ephant Mon?  Did he send you to see me?
Yes he did.
A friend of mine named Tash Kolt sent me a distress call that was jammed at the source. I don't know how serious the situation is, but I want you to find out.
No, but he's mentioned you.
Is there something I can do to help?
He's looking for Tash Kolt.  Do you know where he is?
Tell me where Tash Kolt is now!
Not at the moment.  I know he was having some problems.  Perhaps I can help you...
How?
Doesn't sound like it.
I know he was planning on moving, and that some thugs were looking for him.  If you find him, and those thugs are there, maybe you can help him out.
Great!  Tell me where!
Where should I start?
Here.  I'll add the location to your datapad.  Good luck.
I don't know anyone by that name.  Are you sure you're in the right place?
It's Ok.  I'm a friend of Ephant Mon.
I think you're lying.
Mentioned me in what context?  As a friend?
Yes.
Just as a contact.
What do you suspect?
You have quite the attitude don't you?  Well if you do know Ephant Mon then tell him that I don't deal with your sort.  Perhaps he has other friends he can send to talk to me.
If you've come to apologize then maybe I can help you.
You're right.  I acted rudely.
Apologize?  Forget it.
Start by talking to Hazir Gam'mur in Wayfar.  If anyone knows where Tash is, it will be Hazir.  I'll mark a location on your datapad where Hazir usually hangs out.
I'll get right on it.
Wow!  You unloaded on those guys.  I've never seen anything like it!
Ephant Mon sent me to see how you were doing.
I need to do some things first.
What are you doing?
Good thing you showed up then.  Think you can hang around and keep the thugs off me while I load up my stuff and move out?
Sure thing.
Well, I am kinda busy...
I'm loading up everything I own in the world.  Gotta keep one step ahead of these nerfherders.  I could use your help.
What do you want me to do?
I'm not loading boxes!
Could you just hang around and make sure nobody bothers me while I'm packing?
Sure thing.
Well, I am kinda busy...
Looks like you're too busy to help me. Come back when you're free.
I can't talk now -- I'm waiting for someone else.
I can't believe it! She still loves me! I can't possibly continue in this line of work. I must go to her...
Sorry. The love of my life left me because I'm a mercenary... If there was some hope of her ever taking me back, I would leave this life and become a decent man.

Blood for money. Money for blood. It all seems so stupid now.
Well, come back when you're done.
Messenger! Over here!

No. I have no time for this.

I can't do this right now.

I haven't had time to check up on you, but if you're finished with that work on Corellia you can go see the boss.  Otherwise, get back to work!
Nah, this isn't something Frangee would've had on him.

We need you to go rescue one of our guys before he gets caught.  You do that for us, then maybe I'll tell Borvo that you're clean. So, you wanna help?

Hey, you wanna 'nother job?  Dagorel has said that the gun deal was a big setup.  Get this, he said it was an inside job, too.  It seems that Frangee, one of our guys, was some undercover police guy.  Dagorel says that Frangee is high-tailing it off planet right now, even as we're yappin'.  You wanna make sure he never makes it?

Okay, look... Dagorel's been shot, so he's lost a lot of fluid.  Get out there and lend him a hand while you guys limp back here.  Make sure the police don't catch sight of you.  And if you lead security back here... well, Borvo's gonna be a lot angrier than he already is, got it?

Yeah, I told Borvo you'd do it.  Get out there and make sure that Frangee doesn't make it to his ship.  Make sure it hurts, too.  If it weren't for all the cops around right now, I'd do it myself.  Oh yeah, while you're at it, bring back everything he's got on him in case he's got some more evidence on us.
Then what are you wasting our time for?  Get outta here before we do a little Image Design job on your face!
I thought you had some nerves on you.  Never mind then.  Oh yeah, never mind about talking with Borvo, either.

Well, you see, Borvo had one of his biggest gun sales in a long time to some guys on Corellia.  It turns out it was a setup by the CorSec cops.  Most of our guys are either dead or in jail now, except for Dagorel, Borvo's right hand guy.  He managed to escape, but he's been shot, so he can't make it back here on his own.  That's where you come in.

Frangee was here even longer than me!  He's the one who showed me the ropes around this place.  He was one of Borvo's most trusted guys! To think, he was nothing but a low-down, rotten, womprat snitch!  AARGGG!!!!  Wait a minute.... you're not a cop, are you?  You know what... you take out Frangee and I'll know you ain't one.  Got it?
That's good that you didn't lead them here.  Now get out there and give Dagorel a hand!
What are you waiting for?
I thought I gave you police the slip.  Oh well.  I guess you caught me.
Borvo sent you, right?  I also take it you're going to resist arrest as well.  Sorry it has to be this way.

You let him get killed?  Aarrgh!  Borvo's not gonna be happy when he hears this.  You know, I think you just might get to talk to him after all.  I don't think you'll like what he's gonna say.  Let me go tell Borvo what you did, then I'll let you know.
Then what are you wasting our time for?  Get outta here before we do a little Image Design job on your face!
I thought you had some nerves on you.  Never mind then.  Oh yeah, never mind about talking with Borvo, either.

Good, you got him back safely.  We'll get him patched up right now.  In the meantime, stick around, got it?  Borvo's gonna find out what went down at that sale, and he may need you to do something else for us.  Here's a little something to show you our thanks.

So, did he scream? Serves him right. So, these are the records he was keeping on us, huh?  Ahhh... look here... his badge.  Hey.  Heeeeyyyy.... I've got an idea here.... Yeahhhh, this'll be sweet.  Take this badge, and you head to Corellia.  According to this, it seems that Frangee was going to report back to his Captain at Corsec.  I think he'll still make it.  Isn't that right, Detective Niksel?
Borvo sent you?  You a new guy? No time for that, I guess.  Well, then let's get out of here before the police follow my trail of blood.
Where's Dagorel?  Did you get him back safely?
So did you get him in the back or shoot him in the face?
Nope, you've got the wrong guy.  You may be looking for the other guy nearby who's wounded and dying.
Sure, I'll help.
I hate a snitch.  I'll do it for free.
No thanks, it's not that important to me.
I'm not going against the law.  No thanks.
What's this 'situation'?
How long was Frangee working for Borvo?
Sorry, but I can't do this for you.  You'll need to send one of your own guys.
I've changed my mind.  I can't do this anymore.
No, I had to give the police the slip.  I'll still get him.
I haven't found him yet.
Can't let you in.  Not unless you're willing to do me a favor.
Come back when you are.
Talk to you later.
Borvo needs to get his antique bowl back.  One of our ex-partners took it and took off.  You get it back, give it to me, I'll let you in.
Yeah, he'll send you back over.  Like you pointed out, he's MY buddy.
Corellia.  Try the CorSec offices in Coronet.  I think he got busted.  It's probably in their property stash there.
Cause without going through me, you don't get to see Borvo.
I need somebody to go to Coronet and get something back from the CorSec properties.  A bowl of Borvo's that was stolen.  It's an antique.
Yeah, I guess we will.
Bring me Borvo's Bowl?
Great.  I'll take that, and you can go on in.
What kind of favor?
Maybe I'll try your buddy there.
Where'd this guy take it?
Why don't I just give it to Borvo?
What do you need?
We'll just see about that.
Yeah, I got it.
I'm not ready to give it up yet.
Ok, I have to go.
You wanna talk to me, you talk to my guards.  I don't pay them to let people I don't know bother me.
You don't match the description.  Move along.
Nevermind.  I thought you were someone else.
I'm done with you for now.  Come back some other time and see how I'm doing.
This isn't the necklace I  gave him. Who did you kill?
You wanna talk to me, you talk to my guards.  I don't pay them to let people I don't know bother me.

Well, well... you've helped out old Borvo and brought back his money, have you?  You've got moxy, kid, and I like that.  Not too smart, but bold. *Ho ho ho* You've riled up that officer a good one, though.  He has the Imperials tracking you down, leading them here.  You'll show some respect and clean up your mess, isn't that right?

Look, kid, I like you, but I can't have you on my payroll with the police after you.  I still have something I can use you for, though.  I've had my main man, Dagorel, look into who sent Frangee to us.  It seems it's one of my old partners, who retired from this business a bit back.  I need you to make sure he has a permanent retirement.  Understand?
Good.  I knew you wouldn't disappoint me.  I like you kid.  Now, go out there and take out those Imperials before they even get a sniff of these swamps.  But hey... you already knew that, didn't you?

Yeah, I thought you would. I've asked him to meet me so we can discuss a new venture I'm getting into.  Instead of me meeting him, why don't you introduce him to the business end of your weapon, huh? Do me right, kid, and I might have a little special something for you as a going away present. Hey, while you're at it, get his necklace I gave him when he 'retired'. There's no need for him to have that anymore.
*Ho ho ho* Kid, that was cute.  Did you hear that everyone?  That was cute.  So... where's the punchline, eh?  Because I know you weren't serious........

You're not turning me down, are you?  I think something might be in my ears, because I think I just heard you say you were turning me down.  That's not true, is it?  I'd hate to see what would happen if I actually heard that...

Heh.  As if you didn't know the CorSec Captain called on Imperial help to take care of you.  It seems I've got a hitman running around on Corellia, ain't that right?  I've made this easier for you by having their assault shuttle shot down out of the sky. I even made it look like the Rebels took it out.  But that's a different story.  Ready to leave?

I don't want to believe it myself, but it's the sad truth.  You work with a guy doing a little of this and a little of that, then *BAM*, he turns on you.  What happened to respect? All I ask is for a little respect, but do I get it?  No.  You, on the other hand, you've shown me respect. Let him see what happens when people don't respect me, got it?
Good.  Now do it already.
I like to see a professional in action. I'll step out of your way, because I know you'll get the job done. And you'll get it done in a timely manner, won't you?
You fit the description!  You're under arrest!
Oh no.... he found out, didn't he?  Well, I'm not going out without a fight!
*Ho ho ho* Kid, that was cute.  Did you hear that everyone?  That was cute.  So... where's the punchline, eh?  Because I know you weren't serious........

You're not turning me down, are you?  I think something might be in my ears, because I think I just heard you say you were turning me down.  That's not true, is it?  I'd hate to see what would happen if I actually heard that...

*Ho ho ho* You took them out all by yourself, heh?  You've got the stuff I'm looking for, kid.  You brought me my money, you salvaged the gun deal, got rid of witnesses, and helped to get the cops off my back.... That puts a big smile on my face.  Good job, kid.  You're what I'm looking for.

*Crushes the necklace* I can't believe he double-crossed me. Either way, you've done me good, kid.  I like that, but I can't hire you any longer. In addition to selling guns to interested parties, I keep a few classics for myself. I want you to have an old gun settlers used on Tatooine a long time ago. I got this from my pal, Jabba.  Look, keep in touch kid, okay?
So, have those Imperials been taken care of?
Why haven't you left yet?
You know I will, Borvo.
Yeah, I think I know what you mean.
Haven't I done enough?  No, Borvo, I'm not going to.
No, I'm done with this business.
What mess are we talking about here?
You think your old partner set you up?
I don't think I can handle this anymore.
I've changed my mind, Borvo.  I can't do this.
Not yet.  I'm about to head out to the swamps right now.
Sorry, Borvo, but I was getting my equipment together.
Go ahead and get out of that silly thug suit and back into uniform, Niksel.
Oh... I'm sorry.  Wrong person.
Keep your nose clean.
What? Oh, it's you Niksel. Sorry, no time to talk right now. Don't you have something else you should be doing?
Stop kidding around, Niksel!  I need the evidence.
I don't know who you are, or what you want, but I don't have any time to waste on you.  Be on your way, and keep your nose clean.

Ah, there you are.  Feels good to wear the badge again, doesn't it, Niksel?  How long has it been for you undercover?  6 years now, if I read the report correctly?  Well, I'm glad to finally meet you in person.  Lets cut the banter and get this case closed for you.  I'll send a message over to Aldalad so that he can arrange a pickup point.

Okay, our friend Maerzen has landed in a remote location to throw off Borvo's hitman.  Go out there and pickup the evidence he uncovered, then bring it back to me.  I'll get it over to HQ.  Again, since you're the only person who knows what all of Borvo's men look like, you're the only one we can trust to this.  Are you ready?

Okay, you head out to meet him, then bring him back. Since you're the only one who would be able to recognize Borvo's crew, keep your eyes open.  Aldalad is risking a lot to testify against that Hutt, and I don't want to see him take a hit.  Bring him my way so I can send him down to HQ where it will be safer.

Good.  He's landed a ways from here, so you'll have a bit of a hike.  Fortunately since you've been in contact with him, he'll recognize you on sight, so you don't have to worry about using your codewords.  Once you get the evidence, bring it back right away.

Why?  I know you want to be done with this as much as I do, but it's just about over.  Once we get Aldalad's testimony, we can incarcerate Borvo's scum, then get authority from CorSec and the Queen of Naboo to get rid of that gun-running Hutt!  What's the delay, Niksel?
Well, I'll see if I can get some cadet to pick it up. Hrm...

The same dang thing he was doing when you were 'Frangee'.  After you got him to agree to testify against his company for buying all those illegal weapons, he's been holed up.  Now that you're back, he'll come into the station, but only with you escorting him here, remember?  Ahhhh... you're still in 'role'.  Got it now.  So, you ready?

Detective Maerzen, not Lt. Maerzen.  Ah... still playing the role, eh?  Well, this is serious business and we have no time for that now.  Maerzen has some of the weapons and money we raided during the deal you set up.  For now, you'll just need to pick up the money and bring it back here, so I can get it to HQ.  Got all that?
Don't just stand there, get moving! We don't have time to waste!
Well, get a leg on.  We don't want him out there by himself after Borvo knows what's going on.
The get a move on!  If Borvo's man gets to Maerzen before you... well, I don't even want to think what'll happen to him.
Wait a second... you're not Frangee!  Oh no!  You're a hit man!!!
Niksel, is that you? Huh?? Hey... Oh no!  What have you done to Niksel!!?
What do you mean he left the planet?!  That's ridiculous!
What do you mean you couldn't find him! How did you manager to stay undercover for so long?
Something's fishy here.  I'll call over to CorSec HQ to find out what's going on.  Check back with me in a few.

Why?  I know you want to be done with this as much as I do, but it's just about over.  Once we can get Aldalad's testimony, we can incarcerate Borvo's scum, then have get authority by CorSec and the Queen of Naboo to get rid of that gun-running Hutt!  What's the delay, Niksel?
What?  I don't know what your blathering about, but it's not funny.  You know, maybe you should stop by the cantina to ease up on your nerves.  Get back to me when you've gotten yourself together.

He was dead when you got there!?  Blast it!  Without him, we barely have a case against Borvo.  *Sigh*  Well, let me think.  Maerzin is about to land with all of the guns and money we recovered from that bust.  I'll have to let him know to land elsewhere, just to be on the safe side.  With that evidence, we may still have a case.  Check back with me.

Okay, let me check this.  Yep... looks like it's all here.  Whoa... that is one heck of a lot of money.  Okay, Detective, we have a change in plans.  Maerzen isn't responding back to any calls, and I feel that Borvo's guy got to him after you did.  I'm going to take care of this guy once and for all.  In the meantime, you need to get this money back to HQ.  Whatever you do, don't let Borvo get his hands on it!!!
Have you left yet?
Yeah, what?  And why aren't you gone yet?
Uhh.. yeah, sounds good.  I'll go pick him up.
I'm ready, Captain.
Oh.  Um... actually, I'll have to do that later.
No, I'm afraid he'll sho... er... Borvo's hitman will shoot me.
Aldalad, yes... so... what's he been up to lately?
What evidence was Lt. Maerzen able to recover?
I.. uh... something came up.  I'll meet him later.
I don't want to do any of this anymore.  I feel real bad about this.
No, not yet.  I'm out of here right now, though.
Sorry, I forgot what I wanted to ask you.  I'll get out there on the double.
Huff doesn't want to be disturbed.  He's waiting for his shipment with a Tusken Rifle, and he's not talking to anyone until he finds out what happened to it.
Sorry, Huff's not seeing anyone today.  You'll have to move along.
Come back when you are.
Take it easy.
He's very upset about a Tusken Rifle.  It was an antique, and someone's taken it off the planet.  He wants to get it back, but isn't sure how to go about it.
Huff Darklighter?  The head of the Darklighter estate?  He's only the biggest business magnate on Tatooine.  Where have you been?
We've checked everywhere on Tatooine.  Huff tried some of his contacts on Corellia but they were no help.  Personally I think it's on Naboo.
I hear some criminals got hold of it.  The criminal element has lots to do with these things, when stuff disappears you know?
Well, I suggest you take your head out of the sand and look around you.
Yeah, that guy.  Get it together.  You won't survive long on Tatooine if you can't keep up.
Did you bring the rifle?
Go on in then, and talk to Huff.  He'll be glad to see you.
How come he's not seeing anyone?
Who is Huff?
Where have you looked for the rifle?
What do you know about the rifle?
Don't know him.
Oh, that guy.
Yeah, I got it.
I'm not ready to give it up yet.
Ok, talk to you later.
We're not letting anyone in until the boss gets what he wants.
Come back when you are.
Talk to you later.
He's looking for a tusken Rifle.  Some antique owned by the first king of the Tuskens or something.
Some thieves were arrested in Bestine the other day, claimed to be employees of Borvo the Hutt's.  You know Borvo?
It's an antique.  I think he wants it as an heirloom to hand down to one of his kids.
It was stolen in a shipment that was on it's way to Tatooine.  That's about all I know.
He's a gangster.  Lives on Naboo, I hear, though no one seems to know where.  I would guess the swamps myself.
Just like Jabba.  I hear he and Jabba are friends.  They're always exchanging gifts from what I hear.  I think it's a Hutt thing.
Did you bring the rifle?
Go on in then, and talk to Huff.  He'll be glad to see you.
What is it that he wants?
Know any rumors?
Why does Huff want this rifle?
Where was the rifle?
Don't know Borvo.
He's a Hutt?
Yeah, I got it.
I'm not ready to give it up yet.
Ok, I have to go.
Thanks for your help, friend.  It is fully appreciated.
I wish we had time to chat, but I'm busy.  Maybe another time.
You didn't know Biggs, did you?
I wish we could have had time to chat, but I'm busy. Maybe another time.
Ah, my rifle!  I am amazed that somone has brought it back to me.  You have my friendship and my respect.
You are a good friend to my family, and I appreciate your concern, but there's nothing I need you to do for me right now.  Perhaps you should enjoy this pleasant day, hm?
Please, I don't need this.
Sorry, but I don't know you.  And I don't talk to people I don't know.  It's just not safe anymore now-a-days.  You want to chat, then talk to my guards.

How are you doing, friend.  I want to thank you for recovering my grandfather's gun. I don't know how you got it, and I don't want to know how, either.  I do need your help, though.  About 10 minutes back I got an emergency call from my niece, and she needs help.  I can't run out there, with my leg and all, but will you do it?

I can't believe that slug thinks he can get away with this! If his other activities weren't enough, now he's kidnapping and selling people? Grrr!!!! Okay, friend, even after all you've done, I need your help again. There's a slaver who's waiting for kidnapped people to be shipped off planet that I want you to put a stop to.  Can you do that for me?

Thank you, friend.  Okay, she's out in the desert right now waiting for me to pick her up.  Give her this codephrase 'Biggs is Alive in Spirit', and she'll know I sent you.  From what I understand, she's being hunted down, so keep your eyes peeled.  I'll be here waiting.

Okay, from what my niece has told me, he's out at a designated meeting spot waiting for both the shuttle and the other batch of slaves. He should be caught unawares, so kill him before any of his friends show up. This won't stop Jabba, but it will buy me time to contact the Rebellion for more help.  Good luck, friend.
I can't do it, friend.  I was wounded by a Tusken Raider attack, and my leg is still healing. I hope you'll change your mind, condering how resourceful you are and all.
Are you telling me that you're going to stand aside as Jabba starts up a slavery ring?  I can't believe you'd let that happen!

Well, I don't really understand. She used a special commlink that was for emergency use, but had to cut the conversation short. From what I understand, she and others were kidnapped by some thugs earlier today. She helped the others escape, but she needs help herself.  Will you help, friend?

What doesn't he do is the question you should be asking! What he's doing now is starting up a slave ring. Instead of being content with every other illegal activity, he's kidnapping and selling people as cheap labor!  No one deserves that... heck, not even his own thugs!  Well, some of them... but even still - So, are you going to help?
Well, if you could, try to hurry it up, friend.  You are her only hope.
Hurry, friend. If he makes it offplanet with those slaves, we'll never be able to rescue them.
How can we go on without Biggs?
This is none of your business.  Sorry it's gotta be this way...
Oh no..... first Biggs, and now her.... I don't know if I can go on doing this when everyone around me dies....
He managed to make it off planet with the slaves? *sigh* So many innocent lives lost...
Hold on.  Let me check my maps to see where she should be.  Ask me again in a moment, please.
Let me see if I can track down where he'll be.  Check with me in a few minutes again.
I can't do it, friend.  I was wounded by a Tusken Raider attack, and my leg is still healing. I hope you'll change your mind, condering how resourceful you are and all.
Are you telling me that you're going to stand aside as Jabba starts up a slavery ring?  I can't believe you'd let that happen!

Again, I have to thank you.  You've helped out with family matters again.  I need to talk with my niece after she is able to calm down from the incident. From her crying, I don't like the sound of what I heard. Stick around a bit, if you don't mind.  I may have need of your help even again.

Friend, you've been very helpful, and you've had no reason to. You just walked up and helped someone in need. I greatly admire that. Since you were able to bring me my grandfather's gun, I'd like you to have one of the last things he killed with it. Here's one of my family heirlooms, which is now yours - the skull of the Krayt Dragon that did my old grandpappy in.  The old guy refused to die until it was dead too.  It's yours now, friend.
Yes, that was the codephrase.  Uncle sent you, then?  Thank you so much.  Let's get out of here before Jabba's goons find us.  I need to tell Uncle what Jabba's doing now!
Have you left yet?
Why haven't you stopped Jabba's slaver yet?
Absolutely!  Anything for a Darklighter!
I'll take care of the slaver.
Sorry, I think this is something you should do.  No.
Sorry, I don't interfere with Jabba's plans.
Who is she in trouble with?
What's Jabba doing that's angered you so much?
Sorry Huff, but I can't do this.  Go save her yourself.
Because I'm not going to.  I'm not doing this anymore.
Not yet, but I'm leaving now.
I'm about to right now.
Yes!  This is my rifle!  I can't believe you've found it.  You've certainly earned a place as a friend of the Darklighter family today.  Thank you very much.
Sorry, friend, but this is private property.  You're not going to be allowed to walk around here.
Obviously you don't.  You're not the guy we're testing.
You don't have them?  Yeah, that's what we thought... If you don't have the documents, then
Huff will see you now.   Now that we know we can trust you.  Give him the rifle and you'll have made a very powerful friend.

Sorry, buddy, but you can't just walk in there and talk to Huff.  You need to show him that you're the kind of guy he can trust, which is no easy task.  Maybe if you can get him his grandpappy's gun that was stolen a while back, he might listen.  Last we heard, it was sold to some gun-runner on Naboo.

Well, I'll be!  This is Huff's grandfather's gun, initials and all!  I don't know how you got this back fr- unless...hey - ummm.. I mean - Hey, that's great!  Ummm... Mr. Darklighter has a job that we can't do for him right now.  Do you think you can take these important documents to a contact for us?

Good!  Okay, look.  These are important blueprints, passcodes, and bank account access numbers for the Darklighter estate.  I'll need you to take this to a friend of Mr. Darklighter's whose waiting for them. Jabba would love these plans, but we trust you. Make sure the good guy -er- right guy gets them, okay?
Yeah, that's what I thought.  Well, have a good day.  Hope a Tusken doesn't get ya!

Oh... I... um... have this problem, you see.  I'm... umm... not good with talking to people and when you brought this gun back, I was so overjoyed that Huff will be pleased that I umm... uh, where was I?  Oh, yeah.  I stuttered when I thought you worked for... er... I mean, wanted to work for Huff.  So, are you going to take this te-- do this or not?
Oh, okay.  Sorry about being rude.
Do you have all of the super secret documents?
He's dead?  How did he die?  That's impossible!!!
Darn!  I can't seem to remember where he'd meet you.  Hold on while I find out, then ask me again.
Yeah, that's what I thought.  Well, have a good day.  Hope a Tusken doesn't get ya!

I got word already.  Sorry to have to put you through that, but I thought you were working for those Hutts.  I hope you can understand our need for this test.  Anyways, thank you for the gun.  I've let Huff know that you checked out, and he wants to thank you as well.

Yes, these are the documents.  Hey, will you look at that... you never opened them.  Good.  Well, glad to meet ya, friend. I'll let Huff know that we can trust you after all.  You passed the test.  Head back to Huff's guard, so he can let you in.
What are you hanging around for?
Sure, I'll take them.
Sorry, I won't do your work for you.
Why did you stutter a moment ago?
I've changed my mind.  I don't like where this is going.
I'm about to leave right now.

The Empire, the Rebellion, the Hutts, the Black Sun... my enemies are everywhere. Seems everyone has a vibro-axe to grind for one thing or another that I did in my youth. What are you here for if not to kill me?
Have you found all the ingredients we need?  When you get them, just hand them to me.

Oh so my life is worth something to you, yes? (Just like the old days) If you mean the Zicx bug bomb, I can make it for you. It requires the bile of a mature Sarlacc, and a hearty measure of live Zicx. But... heh... there are no Zicx and no Sarlacc on this planet. You must visit my friend Jowir Ar'Lensa on Tatooine. Give him one of my calling cards and he can help you.
Ah! The Zicx. What mysterious creatures. Did you know that they cannot be killed? Baffling. Now you must acquire the Sarlacc Bile and return with it!
Hideous. Just hideous. Zicx will live forever in this fluid... and they'll hate it! When released, they will wreak havoc on anyone in the area. Return with the Zicx bugs, and be quick!
So you've changed your mind about the weapon? Or... have you aligned yourself with those bloodthirsty thugs?!
Many thanks, friend. Be well... and please forget about me.
Good. Please don't tell anyone that you know of me. I can exchange a very powerful and rare weapon for your silence. Are you interested?
I don't care what you do, just stop bothering me.
You gave me the Zicx, but I still need the Sarlacc bile in order to make your weapon.
You gave me the Sarlacc digestive fluid, but I still need the Zicx to complete your weapon.
Can I have the weapon?
Give me a minute to combine the ingredients...
Don't waste any more of my time then, please.
Return with the Zicx and a jar of Sarlacc bile and I will craft the weapon for you... provided that I'm still alive... and so long as you mention me to no one - anywhere.
I've added the Zicx and the Sarlacc bile to the explosive casing. It's ready for you now.
It's ready, now! Here you go... Remember - you don't know me. You've never heard of me... and you definitely did not get this special weapon from me. Farewell.
Please, don't take too long.  I'm worried that someone will find me.
Sorry, I can't keep doing this work.
I'll go get the Sarlacc Bile for you.
I'll go get the zicx for you.

Like me, he has made many powerful enemies on both sides of the war. Fortunately, his research is valuable to the Hutts - so they're protecting him. He is apparently working on some special process that drastically improves the effectiveness of certain varieties of spice. He lives somewhere in the town of Wayfar... I think.
Here you go... Remember - you don't know me. You've never heard of me... and you definitely did not get this special weapon from me. Farewell.
Relax, old man. I'm just passing through.
I want you to make something for me. A special weapon.

The Zicx Bug Bomb requires the bile of a mature Sarlacc, and a hearty measure of live Zicx. But... heh... there are no Zicx and no Sarlacc on this planet. You must visit my friend Jowir Ar'Lensa on Tatooine. Give him one of my calling cards and he can help you.
I need to be reminded what I'm doing...
I need some more time to get this done.

No idea. Like almost everyone else who gets close to the Sarlacc... you'll likely be killed. However, my friend Jowir knows some other researchers who've managed to survive prolonged contact with the Sarlacc. I have to imagine that they have some special equipment that allows them to get close to it without being destroyed outright. Ask him about them.
No, thanks for offering though.
Oh no! They sent you to kill me didn't they?! I knew that those bloodthirsty thugs would catch up to me some day.
I'll be on my way, then.
Please... begone! I can't keep making these weapons for you. People will find out about me - and then I'll make weapons for NO ONE! Goodbye.
How do I get bile from a Sarlacc?

Go see my friend Jowir Ar'Lensa on Tatooine. You'll find him hiding out in Wayfar - protected by the Hutts. He is researching insects to help enhance spice production... so they keep him safe. Give him my calling card. Tell him that you want the Zicx and he will help you.
Sounds good. Where do I start?
No thanks. Like I said, I'm just passing through.
What is this? I can't use this. I only need the Zicx bugs and the Sarlacc bile to make the weapon.
What bloodthirsty thugs are you talking about?
What is this weapon?
Where can I find Jowir on Tatooine?
Yes, I've changed my mind.

The infamous Zicx grenade. Outlawed by the Empire, reviled by the Alliance... and coveted by the Hutts and Black Sun. I still have many of the original explosive case prototypes. The critical components are missing, though. I need a bunch of live Zicx and a jar of Sarlacc bile. Together with the special firing mechanism and casing, I'll craft an outstanding weapon for you.

The Sarlacc is a gruesome, omnivorous, immobile beast almost entirely concealed beneath the desert sands. Only its foul mouth extends to the surface, ringed with grasping tentacles ready to pull any prey unfortunate to fall into the shifting sands. Because of its isolation, the Sarlacc rarely feeds, as it must rely on animals that stumble into the pit. As such, it has evolved an extremely efficient digestive process. According to lore, the stomach pit of the Sarlacc keeps its prey alive for a thousand years, slowly dissolving its meal into needed nutrients, while the hapless victim is kept alive in searing, endless agony.

With several enemy camps on Dathomir, Captain Sarguillo of the Aurilian village has asked you to scout out the locations of these camps.  They could be located anywhere on Dathomir.  Each camp has a shield generator that must be powered down remotely before you can infiltrate the camp.  In order to find the frequency codes for the various shield generators in use at the enemy camps, you must hunt down members of the enemy force and relieve them of any frequence code datadisks they might be carrying.  If you return such a datadisk to Captain Sarguillo, he will give you a remote control configured for the frequency code on the disk.  You may then use this remote to power down the corresponding shield. 

Once you have a remote control device (or you are grouped with someone who has one),  you may attempt to capture the camp's commander.   There are two ways to earn credit for this mission:

Option 1:  Power down the shield generator and eliminate at least 5 of the enemy's troops afterwards - that should be enough to lure the commander out.  You will also be made personally responsible for making sure the commander gets back safely to Aurilia.  If you perish any time after the shield comes down but before the commander is captured, i.e. you will need to complete 'Option 2' below, instead of allowing one of your group mates to take on that responsibility. 

Option 2:  Join a group with someone who powered down the shield generator and capture the commander.  You must then safely return him to Captain Sarguillo for questioning. 

Since the Aurilians value teamwork and comraderie so greatly, you will receive a mission bonus from Captain Sarguillo if you complete this mission with a friend.  To become eligible for the bonus, one of you must power down the shield and one of you must capture the commander. 

Remember that the mission is not complete for any participant until the commander is safely returned to the Aurilian village.

This weapon cannot kill and only works on animals.

A spur fashioned from natural organics.  A knowledgable scout can throw this at an enemy creature, placing it in a perfect spot to cause pain.  This has the effect of damaging the creature's mind.  However, the effects are never fatal.

A small cannister packed with a fine and somewhat sticky mesh.  When it strikes the target, the mesh entangles them making movement more difficult.  This has the effect of making the target easier to hit with melee attacks.

Similar to the wire mesh trap, but this trap has been enhanced.  The wire mesh has been strengthened and treated with a bioluminescent goo.  The target will become easier to hit with both melee and ranged attacks.

A special device that emits annoying noises.  When thrown at a creature by a sufficiently skilled scout, the trap will cause the target to become stunned.  The raw shock of the noise will also cause a large amount of damage to the target's mind pool.
A small container of natural bioluminescent liquid.  Splashing the target with this substance has the effect of making the target easier to hit with ranged attacks.

The sonic pulse is a small bomb activated by impact.  When triggered, it emits an extremely powerful pulse of sonic energy.  This has the result of stunning and dizzying any creatures caught within its effective radius.

A small container filled with the natural musk of an animal.  The musk has a repellent smell and can cause a target to become distracted.  This has the effect of making the target more vulnerable to status effects like stun or intimidate.

A small Phecnacine tranquililzer delivery system.  This object is thrown at a target in combat.  When it strikes something, it releases a thin mist of poison.  The poison will cause the target's movement to slow significantly.

A trap containing some form of compressed mucilage based adhesive.  This trap is thrown at a target creature.  If the adhesive mesh successfully traps the creature, the target will become immobile for a short time and will suffer significant damage to its action pool.

This is an Anti Decay Kit which can make an item not decay when a player dies or uses the item.  To use the Anti Decay Kit, both the Kit and the item you want to use the Kit on must be in your inventory.  Place the item inside the Kit by dragging and dropping the item onto the Anti Decay Kit.  Use the radial menu option on the Kit called Apply Anti Decay to make the item not decay.  If you change your mind, you can retrieve the item by selecting the radial menu option Retrieve Item From Kit.   Only items that can be insured are valid to be used with the Anti Decay Kit.  Items that are weapons are also valid to be used with the Anti Decay Kit.
